text:
pagerduty-bot: INC00018321 triggered — Dedicated pool 'resv-eu-1' high queue depth. Severity: P1. Paging oncall Natasha (oncall).
Natasha (oncall): acked. jumping in — what's the signal? :rotating_light:
ops-bot: Alert summary: queue_length > 1200 (5m avg), enqueue rate spike +420% from ACME-CORP tenant. Autoscaler state: stalled, last scaling event 03:12 UTC.
Siva (infra): looking at autoscaler logs now — seeing repeated errors: 
```
ERROR scaler: cannot provision nodes: reached global_quota_limit (max_pools=8, pool_id=resv-eu-1)
WARN scaler: backoff applying 1m
```
Natasha (oncall): so autoscaler hit a quota ceiling, not failing open. Can we bypass for emergency?
Jordan (eng-runtime): autoscaler is intentionally capped due to reservations limits. We can do manual scale if infra ok — but need to check GPU quota and reservation alignment.
Meera (support): Carla on the ACME side is reporting increased 429s and long queue times; their SLA dashboards show 30% request failures starting ~02:45 UTC.
Carla (customer-success): ACME says impact is customer-facing for their inference endpoint (batching -> throttle). They just opened a support ticket. Need ETA to restore.
Siva (infra): quick inventory: resv-eu-1 has 28 dedicated GPUs allocated, all in use. There are idle GPUs in shared pools but routing policy forbids live spillover for reserved customers.
Natasha (oncall): immediate options: 1) manual emergency scale of resv-eu-1 up to 36 GPUs (requires quota bump), 2) evict noisy sessions from resident tenants, 3) apply tenant-level concurrency throttle for ACME to reduce queue growth, 4) failover some ACME traffic to hosted region eu-central-1 if possible.
Jordan (eng-runtime): to add — runtime has a noisy-session eviction endpoint: `/admin/evict_sessions?pool=resv-eu-1&threshold=cpu` — we can evict long-running low-priority sessions. Will run dry-run first.
Natasha (oncall): do dry-run eviction now, call it out in channel before actual.
Siva (infra): executing dry-run: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/admin/evict_sessions -d 'pool=resv-eu-1&dry_run=true'` -> response: 142 candidates (est reclaim 3 GPUs).
Jordan (eng-runtime): that only yields 3 GPUs — not enough for the 12 GPU shortfall. Dry-run looks safe.
Natasha (oncall): Meera/Carla — need to give ACME a temporary concurrency cap. Meera please ask customer if 20% request throttling acceptable for next 30m while we patch.
Meera (support): on a call with ACME now. They're willing to accept reduced concurrency for 30m if it avoids errors. I'll confirm.
ops-bot: Action log: manual scale request created (request_id=scale-REQ-8592), pending quota approval.
Siva (infra): I can request emergency quota bump from infra quota service but it requires approval from infra leads; pinging @infra-leads.
Natasha (oncall): while we wait, let's apply tenant throttle. Jordan, what's the quickest config change?
Jordan (eng-runtime): change is simple — update tenant QoS: `PATCH /config/tenants/ACME-CORP` body `{\n  "concurrency_limit": 0.2\n}` — will take effect first routing tick (~8s).
Natasha (oncall): Meera, go ahead and warn ACME this will throttle them to 20% concurrency, brief maintenance window.
Meera (support): telling them now. ACME replied: "do it, prefer stable with throttles over 500s".
Natasha (oncall): applying throttle now. `curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/tenants/ACME-CORP -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"concurrency_limit":0.2}'`
ops-bot: Config change applied by Natasha (oncall). Event: tenant-qos-update (ACME-CORP)
Jordan (eng-runtime): seeing immediate drop in enqueue rate from ACME by ~62% in 30s. Queue depth still high but stabilizing.
Siva (infra): quota approval still pending. Infra leads asked for impact numbers before approval. Need current RPS and queue headroom.
Natasha (oncall): posting quick metrics: `ACME enqueue 5m: 1200/s -> 460/s after throttle. Queue depth: 1230 -> 780. Latency p95: 5.8s -> 3.4s`.
Carla (customer-success): ACME thanks us for quick action. They're reporting fewer 5xx but still elevated latency for batched jobs.
Jordan (eng-runtime): also seeing autoscaler logs: 
```
INFO scaler: target_nodes=36 requested
ERROR cloud: quota check failed: quota_exceeded (requested 8 GPUs, available 0)
```
Siva (infra): quota system denies because pool-level cap is enforced to prevent noisy neighbor stealing. We need an override. I'm escalating to infra-leads for emergency override.
Natasha (oncall): in parallel, can we spill some reserved jobs to shared pool as a temporary fallback? What are risks?
Jordan (eng-runtime): technically doable: route matching ACME tenant to a compatible hosted model variant in shared pool with lower priority. Risk: data isolation concerns — ACME is enterprise, they require resv isolation. Need ACME consent.
Meera (support): ACME explicitly cannot have shared termination due to compliance. They said no to spillover.
Natasha (oncall): okay, no spill. Continue throttle + eviction. Siva, any chance to reclaim GPUs by evicting noisy tenant(s)?
Siva (infra): checking allocation map — Tenant 'sparkle-ai' is running many low-util long sessions; they aren't reserved but occupy dedicated nodes due to a config mismatch. We can evict those sessions and enforce pool-affinity corrections.
Jordan (eng-runtime): recommend targeted eviction: identify sessions with idle score < 0.1 & runtime > 20m. I'll run selection and then evict.
Siva (infra): selection returns 9 nodes worth of reclaimable GPUs if we evict their sessions — that'll cover the shortfall. Need confirmation to evict non-reserved tenant sessions in resv-eu-1.
Natasha (oncall): proceed. Prioritize minimal customer-facing breakage; these are non-reserved long-running dev sessions. Go for it.
Siva (infra): executing eviction: `POST /admin/evict_sessions?pool=resv-eu-1&filter=tenant:sparkle-ai&force=true` -> reclaimed 9 GPUs, nodes drained gracefully over 45s.
ops-bot: Eviction completed — 9 GPUs reclaimed. Pool utilization now 87% -> 55% used.
Jordan (eng-runtime): autoscaler sees new headroom and attempts to scale down, but we can now consider scaling up allocations to ACME if needed.
Meera (support): ACME confirms error rate dropped to 3% and latency improving. They appreciate us, flagged as 'major incident' on their side but stabilized.
Natasha (oncall): good. Logging immediate mitigation steps. Next: follow-ups — (1) postmortem on why autoscaler quota locked us out, (2) fix dev sessions pool-affinity bug that allowed non-reserved tenants to land on reserved GPUs, (3) shorter-term: add emergency override process for infra leads, (4) revisit routing policies for critical enterprise tenants.
Carla (customer-success): I'll coordinate customer comms and update ACME with timeline and RCA when ready.
Siva (infra): I've created infra ticket INF-4297 to request permanent quota increase & add automation to detect pool-gridlock patterns.
Jordan (eng-runtime): created runtime PR to tighten pool-affinity checks and add preemptive eviction heuristics: PR#5423.
Natasha (oncall): closing the pager for now — system stabilized, ACME accepts throttles and evictions. Leaving a bridge open for 60m for monitoring. If any regressions, reactivate.
ops-bot: Incident INC00018321 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Bridge: https://zoom.internal/bridge/INC00018321.
Meera (support): ACME will keep monitoring; they want a follow-up call tomorrow.
Natasha (oncall): thanks everyone. Postmortem owner assigned: Jordan (eng-runtime). ETA draft in 48h.
Carla (customer-success): noting customer impact: ACME experienced 30% request failures for ~45m before mitigation, no data loss, SLA impact under review.
Natasha (oncall): end-of-thread notes: tag follow-ups: #postmortem #quota #noisy-neighbor #customer-impact. :white_check_mark:
